newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X companies still have cash - Price Waterhouse.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X companies still have cash - Price Waterhouse.

text.p: Gold prospector Bre-X Minerals Ltd still has millions of dollars in its coffers, despite being under creditor protection after the infamous Busang gold salting scandal, said the firm monitoring its accounts.
In a report filed with a Canadian court this week, Price Waterhouse Ltd said Bre-X and sister firms Bresea Resources Ltd and Bro-X Minerals Ltd had a combined C$35.9 million in cash at May 31.
The Calgary-based companies headed by David Walsh also had net working capital, or current assets minus liabilities, of C$35.9 million at the end of May, the report said.
The report was the first filed by Price Waterhouse, which was appointed monitor of the firms under Canada's Companies' Creditors Arrangement Act (CCAA).
The legislation allows protection from creditors and the reorganization of insolvent firms under court supervision.

Bre-X faces a spate of lawsuits filed by Canadian and U.S. shareholders after the Busang gold play in Indonesia -- once touted as the biggest find this century -- was deemed in early May to be an unprecendented fraud.
The revelation wiped out the value of Bre-X shares, which once traded above C$250 before a 10-for-1 split.

In its report, Price Waterhouse listed 11 lawsuits filed against Bre-X, its related companies and several officers and dirctors over alleged negligence, misrepresentation and fraud, but did not give an estimated total amount for which they are being sued.

In May, Bre-X filed complaints with the Royal Canadian Mounted Police and Indonesia police regarding what Bre-X Chief Executive Walsh described as a fraud perpetrated against the company involving widespread tampering with drilling samples.
Price Waterhouse also said it and Forensic Investigative Associates Inc were hired by Bre-X to investigate the crime. Investigations were continuing, it said.
The accounting firm said its report did not contain any audited or otherwise independently verified information.
Instead, it included results of inquiries and discussions in Canada and Indonesia and analysis of financial data prepared by the companies.
The report said the monthly cost of running the companies' offices in Calgary and Jakarta -- whose staff were cut dramatically after the salting revelation -- was estimated at C$164,000.
Bre-X, Bresea and Bro-X stock is not currently allowed to trade in any jurisdiction.
